items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: I think it's important to mention the fact that he and -- what the heck was that big black rock 'n roll drummer in New York in the very early stages of rock, one of his rhythm and blues -- Panama Francis.

ctx.x: His parents used to bring him, he and the rest of the family in Connecticut in the (inaudible) late '40s. But I think it's rather -- from an information standpoint, I think it's important to mention the fact that he and -- what the heck was that big
black rock 'n roll drummer in New York in the very early stages of rock, one of his rhythm and blues -- Panama Francis.

items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: Yeah, Nat Cole, Woody Herman -- remember Woody Herman and his small group?

ctx.x: Some beautiful days, man. I tell you. I really enjoyed my association with him and seeing so many artists down there; remember Nat Cole came down one time?
Yeah, Nat Cole, Woody Herman -- remember Woody Herman and his small group?
Yeah. With Shelly Manne, Ernie Royal, Milt Jackson.
